postTitle: Unmarried Couples: Building the Protections Marriage Gives
topic: Twelve years of half the mortgage, and one name on the flat

assumptions.notes: No euro figures. Illustrative couple from the post: Sofia and Lena, together twelve years, never married, no wills. The flat is in Lena's name, bought before they met; Sofia has paid half of every mortgage payment. Lena dies in an accident at 41. In many countries the flat passes to Lena's parents, Sofia has no automatic right to stay, her payments are legally generosity, and Lena's pension pays nothing because the rules name a spouse, and the hospital speaks to Lena's mother. This reel: a will, a recorded ownership share and powers of attorney could have changed much of it; formalising a share may need legal advice and extra costs. Rules vary by country. Not legal advice.

Powers of attorney for money and health, so each partner can act and decide for the other.
One page recording Sofia's share of the flat. Contributions nobody wrote down are hard to prove.
And one will, in the form local law requires. Where forced heirship applies, it can still give the free part.

caption.instagram:
Twelve years paying half the mortgage. In many countries, legally, that was generosity.

Sofia and Lena, an illustrative couple, have been together twelve years. The flat is in Lena's name; Sofia has paid half of every mortgage payment. Neither has a will. If Lena dies, in many countries the flat passes to her parents, Sofia has no automatic right to stay, and the hospital may speak to Lena's mother, not to Sofia.

A will, a recorded ownership share and powers of attorney could have changed much of what followed. Formalising an ownership share may need legal advice, lender consent and extra costs. For any shared home, the question is the same: if one of us dies, does that share go to the other, or to the heirs?
